details:
- CVE-2026-70461: count a trailing backslash when sizing the implied-include
  filter rule, so a --files-from entry ending in a backslash can no longer
  write one attacker-controlled byte past the rule's heap allocation
- CVE-2026-70456: reserve the slot read_args() needs for its trailing NULL, so
  a peer argument count landing exactly on maxargs cannot write one pointer
  past the argv allocation
- CVE-2026-70458: refuse FLAG_HLINKED when hard links are not in use and on a
  directory entry, so a peer cannot displace the checksum slot through
  hard-link extras that were never reserved; gate the hard-link basis check on
  S_ISREG(file->mode) so a hard-linked symlink or device cannot read a checksum
  slot it never had; also set sender_keeps_checksum in the daemon-as-sender
  path so %C cannot log adjacent heap
- CVE-2026-70462: reject a non-positive MSG_IO_TIMEOUT from the peer and cap it
  at 24 hours, and make set_io_timeout()'s arithmetic overflow-safe, so a
  crafted server can neither disable the client's --timeout nor spin it at 100%
  CPU on a negative select() timeout
- CVE-2026-70453: bound the hash_search() chain walk at MAX_CHAIN_LEN, so a
  basis file whose weak checksums all collide cannot drive an
  O(file_size * chain_length) scan
- CVE-2026-53785: create each implied parent directory through do_mkdir_at()
  against a held O_NOFOLLOW directory fd, so a parent component raced into a
  symlink can no longer place --relative directories outside the destination
- CVE-2026-53794: reject --max-alloc=0, which disabled the per-allocation size
  cap entirely instead of enforcing a zero one
- CVE-2026-53790: shell-escape %VAR% expansions for their quoting context in
  the daemon's exec hooks and refuse a peer value holding shell syntax, quote
  the program names the rsync-ssl helper execs, and widen the remote-shell
  safe_arg() escape set
